methods.label: Express every volume using the common radius
methods.explanation:
Let the common radius be \(r>0\). The sphere's diameter is \(2r\), so this is also the height of the cone and cylinder. Using one variable makes their volumes easy to compare:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac13\pi r^2(2r)=\frac23\pi r^3,\\
M&=\pi r^2(2r)=2\pi r^3,\\
C&=\frac43\pi r^3.
\end{aligned}
\]
The cone and sphere volumes add to
\[
A+C=\left(\frac23+\frac43\right)\pi r^3
=2\pi r^3=M.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{A-M+C=0}\), choice A.
